ei.title: Volunteering at an Animal Sanctuary by Mia Watson
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: Volunteering at an Animal Sanctuary by Mia Watson As the leader of our school club Care for Animals, I organized a volunteer trip to an animal sanctuary for my club members. An animal sanctuary is a special place where rescued, injured, or abused animals can live in a safe and caring environment. All the club members and I agreed that the sanctuary would be the perfect place to learn about animal care. Excited for a new experience, we set out to volunteer. July 29, Monday Our club arrived at the Free Animals sanctuary. Jane, the staff member in charge of animal care, welcomed us with a big smile and gave us a tour of the facility. It was amazing to see bears and elephants moving freely in a large field. Our tasks for the day included cleaning the shelter and preparing food for the animals. While cleaning the habitats, we checked if there were any hazards that could harm the animals. Then, we helped prepare the food by cutting up fruits and vegetables and dividing them into several large baskets. For old elephants with weak teeth, we chopped bananas instead of the sugarcane that they usually eat. Spending the whole day helping out with the animals was an incredible experience for me. It was a rewarding experience, and I was impressed with the attention the staff members gave to all the animals. July 30, Tuesday Today, we did something special for Ben and Lily. These two baby bears were rescued after they had been raised illegally in a tiny cage on a farm for many years. To help the bears restore their natural instincts, we carried out some special activities known as “behavioral enrichment.” For example, we made honey-log feeders for the bears. First, we made several holes in a log and filled them with honey. Then, we hung the honey-log feeders on trees near the bears’ habitat. As bears are intelligent and curious creatures, they can become bored and stressed when lacking mental and physical stimulation. The honey-log feeders stimulate their natural curiosity and keep them as active as they would be in the wild. After a while, Ben and Lily approached the feeders and started eating the honey inside. They are so cute! July 31, Wednesday This morning, we had the opportunity to learn about animal treatment thanks to Molly, an elderly elephant. After spending 25 years carrying tourists along rough roads, she developed a twisted spine and foot pain. In order to support Jane in taking care of Molly’s foot, we took part in positive reinforcement training, which involves using rewards to encourage desirable behaviors. When I gently touched her foot with a pole and called out, “foot,” she lifted it. We then rewarded her with a sweet piece of watermelon, her favorite fruit. This training helps reduce the stress that animals experience during controlled situations, such as treatment or a health examination. The good news is Molly seems to be adapting well, and I expect her to get better soon. August 1, Thursday On the last day, we were called to the rescue center due to a sudden emergency. Some dehydrated birds had fallen out of the sky in the city and were brought to the center. Following the veterinarian’s guidance, we provided water to the birds while the vets treated their broken wings and legs and injected them with vitamins for a speedy recovery. It was shocking that this type of accident happens every year since the high temperatures dry up water sources in the city. Caring for the birds, I couldn’t help but reflect on the impact of human activities on climate change and how it harms animals. Saying goodbye to the animals and staff, I felt grateful for the opportunity to volunteer. From this experience, I learned the importance of treating animals with respect and care. I also came to realize that humans are just another kind of animal and share the Earth with all other living creatures. To improve animal welfare, I’ll work hard with Care for Animals members. Hopefully, I’ll have the chance to volunteer at another sanctuary next summer.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: welcome → welcomed. 주어 Jane + 과거시제
det.analysis:
① welcome ❌ — 주어가 Jane(3인칭 단수)이고 과거의 일을 말하므로 과거시제 동사 welcomed(맞이했다)가 맞아요. 원형 welcome은 틀려요 ←정답

② to see ✅ — 'It was amazing to see ~'는 진짜 주어(to see)를 뒤로 보낸 가주어 It 구문이라 to부정사 to see가 맞아요.

③ checked ✅ — 'we checked ~(우리가 확인했다)'는 과거시제로 맞아요.

④ cutting ✅ — 'by cutting up ~(자름으로써)'은 전치사 by 뒤라서 동명사 cutting이 맞아요.
det.tip: 과거에 일어난 일이고 주어가 Jane이라 동사는 과거형 welcomed. 원형 welcome은 못 써요.

questions.passage: Then, we ①<u>helped</u> prepare the food by cutting up fruits and vegetables and ②<u>divided</u> them into several large baskets.  For old elephants with weak teeth, we ③<u>chopped</u> bananas instead of the sugarcane that they usually eat.  Spending the whole day ④<u>helping</u> out with the animals was an incredible experience for me.  It was a rewarding experience, and I was impressed with the attention the staff members gave to all the animals.  July 30, Tuesday Today, we did something special for Ben and Lily.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: divided → dividing. by + 동명사 병렬(cutting and dividing)
det.analysis:
① helped ✅ — 'we helped prepare ~(우리는 준비하는 것을 도왔다)'는 과거시제 동사로 맞아요.

② divided ❌ — 'by cutting up ~ and dividing ~(자르고 나누면서)'처럼 by 뒤에서 cutting과 나란히 이어지므로 동명사 dividing이 맞아요. 과거형 divided를 쓰면 앞의 cutting과 짝이 안 맞아 틀려요 ←정답

③ chopped ✅ — '바나나를 잘게 잘랐다'는 과거시제로 맞아요.

④ helping ✅ — 'Spending the whole day helping out ~(하루 종일 도우며 보낸)'은 앞의 동명사구를 꾸미는 분사라 맞아요.
det.tip: by cutting ~ and dividing ~ 처럼 and로 이어지면 앞(cutting)과 형태를 맞춰 dividing.

questions.passage: August 1, Thursday On the last day, we were called to the rescue center due to a sudden emergency.  Some dehydrated birds ①<u>had fallen</u> out of the sky in the city and were brought to the center.  Following the veterinarian’s guidance, we provided water to the birds while the vets treated their broken wings and legs and ②<u>injected</u> them with vitamins for a speedy recovery.  It was shocking that this type of accident ③<u>happens</u> every year since the high temperatures dry up water sources in the city. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: Said → Saying. 분사구문(내가 인사하며) = 능동 현재분사
det.analysis:
① had fallen ✅ — 새들이 센터로 옮겨지기 '전에' 떨어진 일이라 과거완료 had fallen이 맞아요.

② injected ✅ — 'the vets treated ~ and injected ~(수의사들이 치료하고 주사했다)'처럼 treated와 나란히 이어지는 과거시제라 맞아요.

③ happens ✅ — 주어가 'this type of accident(이런 종류의 사고, 단수)'라서 단수동사 happens가 맞아요.

④ Said ❌ — 'Saying goodbye ~, I felt ~'는 '작별 인사를 하면서'라는 뜻의 분사구문이에요. 내가 직접 인사하는 능동이라 현재분사 Saying이 맞아요. 과거분사 Said는 '말해진'이라는 수동이 되어 틀려요 ←정답
det.tip: 분사구문에서 '내가 ~하면서'처럼 능동이면 현재분사(-ing). Saying goodbye = 작별하면서.

questions.passage: To help the bears ①<u>restore</u> their natural instincts, we carried out some special activities known as “behavioral enrichment. ” For example, we made honey-log feeders for the bears.  First, we made several holes in a log and ②<u>filled</u> them with honey.  Then, we hung the honey-log feeders on trees near the bears’ habitat.  As bears are ③<u>foolish</u> and curious creatures, they can become bored and stressed when lacking mental and physical stimulation.  The honey-log feeders ④<u>stimulate</u> their natural curiosity and keep them as active as they would be in the wild.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: foolish → intelligent. 곰은 지적이고 호기심 많은 동물
det.analysis:
① restore(회복하다) ✅ — 곰의 타고난 본능을 '회복시키도록' 돕는다는 문맥에 맞아요.

② filled(채웠다) ✅ — 통나무 구멍에 꿀을 '채웠다'는 문맥에 맞아요.

③ foolish(어리석은) ❌ — 곰이 먹이통을 궁금해하고 다가가는 걸 보면 '지적이고 호기심 많은(intelligent and curious)' 동물이에요. 원문은 intelligent(똑똑한)라야 뒤 내용과 이어져요. foolish(어리석은)는 정반대라 틀려요 ←정답

④ stimulate(자극하다) ✅ — 먹이통이 곰의 타고난 호기심을 '자극한다'는 문맥에 맞아요.
det.tip: 뒤에 curious(호기심 많은)와 나란히 오고, 곰이 먹이통을 탐구하므로 intelligent(똑똑한)가 맞아요.

questions.passage: July 31, Wednesday This morning, we had the opportunity to learn about animal treatment thanks to Molly, an ①<u>elderly</u> elephant.  After spending 25 years carrying tourists along rough roads, she developed a twisted spine and foot pain.  In order to support Jane in taking care of Molly’s foot, we took part in positive reinforcement training, which involves using rewards to ②<u>discourage</u> desirable behaviors.  When I gently touched her foot with a pole and called out, “foot,” she lifted it.  We then ③<u>rewarded</u> her with a sweet piece of watermelon, her favorite fruit.  This training helps ④<u>reduce</u> the stress that animals experience during controlled situations, such as treatment or a health examination.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: discourage → encourage. 보상으로 좋은 행동을 '장려'
det.analysis:
① elderly(나이 든) ✅ — Molly가 25년을 일한 '나이 든' 코끼리라는 문맥에 맞아요.

② discourage(단념시키다) ❌ — 보상(rewards)을 주는 것은 바람직한 행동을 '장려하기(encourage)' 위한 거예요. discourage(못 하게 하다)는 정반대라 틀려요 ←정답

③ rewarded(보상했다) ✅ — 발을 든 Molly에게 수박으로 '보상했다'는 문맥에 맞아요.

④ reduce(줄이다) ✅ — 이 훈련이 통제된 상황에서 동물의 스트레스를 '줄여' 준다는 문맥에 맞아요.
det.tip: using rewards to encourage ~ = 보상으로 ~을 장려하다. discourage면 반대 뜻이 돼요.

questions.passage: Caring for the birds, I couldn’t help but reflect on the impact of human activities on climate change and how it harms animals.  Saying goodbye to the animals and staff, I felt grateful for the opportunity to volunteer.  From this experience, I learned the importance of treating animals with respect and care.  I also came to realize that humans are just another kind of animal and share the Earth with all other living creatures.  To improve __________, I’ll work hard with Care for Animals members.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: To improve __ = animal welfare(동물 복지)를 개선하려는 다짐
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞뒤에서 글쓴이는 동물을 존중·보살피는 법을 배웠고(learned the importance of treating animals with respect and care) '이것을 개선하기 위해 열심히 하겠다'고 다짐해요. 봉사 글 전체가 동물을 위한 것이에요.

✅ ① animal welfare(동물 복지) — 동물을 더 잘 대하려는 다짐과 딱 맞아요 ←정답

❌ ② school grades(학교 성적) — 성적 이야기는 글에 없어요.

❌ ③ tourism income(관광 수입) — 오히려 관광에 이용된 코끼리를 안타까워해요.

❌ ④ farming skills(농사 기술) — 농사 기술과는 관련이 없어요.
det.tip: 결론의 '동물을 존중·보살피며 대하는 것의 중요성'과 이어지는 말 = animal welfare.

questions.passage: July 31, Wednesday This morning, we had the opportunity to learn about animal treatment thanks to Molly, an elderly elephant.  After spending 25 years carrying tourists along rough roads, she developed a twisted spine and foot pain.  In order to support Jane in taking care of Molly’s foot, we took part in positive reinforcement training, which involves using rewards to encourage __________.  When I gently touched her foot with a pole and called out, “foot,” she lifted it.  We then rewarded her with a sweet piece of watermelon, her favorite fruit.  This training helps reduce the stress that animals experience during controlled situations, such as treatment or a health examination.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: encourage __ = desirable behaviors(바람직한 행동)
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에 '보상을 사용해 ~을 장려하는(using rewards to encourage ~)'이 나와요. 보상을 주면 어떤 행동을 늘리려는 걸까요? 바로 '바람직한 행동'이에요.

❌ ① aggressive reactions(공격적 반응) — 보상으로 공격성을 키우진 않아요.

❌ ② random movements(무작위 움직임) — 특정한 좋은 행동을 유도하는 것이지 아무 움직임이 아니에요.

✅ ③ desirable behaviors(바람직한 행동) — 보상으로 좋은 행동을 이끌어낸다는 흐름에 맞아요 ←정답

❌ ④ physical punishments(체벌) — 보상(reward)과 정반대예요.
det.tip: rewards(보상)로 유도하는 것 = 바람직한 행동(desirable behaviors).

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 과일·채소를 잘라서 나눴다 → '통째로'는 불일치
det.analysis:
① ✅ 일치 — 'Jane ~ welcomed us with a big smile and gave us a tour'에서 미소로 맞이하고 시설을 견학시켜 주었다고 했어요.

② ✅ 일치 — 'It was amazing to see bears and elephants moving freely in a large field'와 맞아요.

③ ✅ 일치 — 'Our tasks ~ included cleaning the shelter and preparing food'와 맞아요.

❌ ④ 불일치 — 'cutting up fruits and vegetables and dividing them into several large baskets'에서 과일과 채소를 '잘라서' 바구니에 나눴어요. 자르지 않고 통째로 담았다는 진술은 사실과 달라요 ←정답
det.tip: cutting up ~(잘게 자르다)이 핵심. 통째로 담은 게 아니에요.

ch: Jane은 미소를 지으며 봉사자들을 맞이하고 시설을 견학시켜 주었다.
봉사자들은 곰과 코끼리가 넓은 들판에서 자유롭게 움직이는 것을 보았다.
그날 봉사자들의 임무에는 축사 청소와 먹이 준비가 포함되었다.
봉사자들은 과일과 채소를 자르지 않고 통째로 여러 바구니에 나누어 담았다.

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 통나무에 구멍 뚫고 꿀 채워 나무에 매달았다 = 일치
det.analysis:
✅ ① 일치 — 'we made several holes in a log and filled them with honey. Then, we hung the honey-log feeders on trees'와 맞아요 ←정답

❌ ② 불일치 — Ben과 Lily는 야생이 아니라 농장의 좁은 우리에서 불법으로 길러졌어요(raised illegally in a tiny cage on a farm).

❌ ③ 불일치 — 곰은 자극이 부족하면 지루하고 스트레스를 받는다고 했어요(become bored and stressed when lacking ~ stimulation).

❌ ④ 불일치 — 먹이통은 식욕을 떨어뜨리는 게 아니라 호기심을 자극하고 활동적으로 유지해 줘요(stimulate ~ curiosity and keep them ~ active).
det.tip: made holes ~ filled with honey ~ hung on trees. ②③④는 본문과 반대.

ch: 봉사자들은 통나무에 구멍을 뚫고 꿀을 채워 나무에 매달았다.
Ben과 Lily는 야생에서 태어나 곧바로 보호구역으로 왔다.
곰은 충분한 자극이 없어도 지루함을 느끼지 않는다.
먹이통은 곰의 식욕을 떨어뜨려 활동을 줄이는 역할을 한다.

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 훈련은 스트레스를 줄임(reduce) → '키운다'는 불일치
det.analysis:
① ✅ 일치 — 'After spending 25 years carrying tourists ~, she developed a twisted spine and foot pain'과 맞아요.

❌ ② 불일치 — 'This training helps reduce the stress ~'에서 훈련은 스트레스를 '줄여' 줘요. 스트레스를 키운다는 진술은 정반대라 틀려요 ←정답

③ ✅ 일치 — 'When I gently touched her foot with a pole and called out, "foot," she lifted it'과 맞아요.

④ ✅ 일치 — 'high temperatures dry up water sources ~ this type of accident happens every year'와 맞아요.
det.tip: reduce the stress(스트레스를 줄이다)가 핵심. 키운다는 건 반대예요.

ch: Molly는 25년 동안 관광객을 태우고 다닌 뒤 척추가 뒤틀리고 발에 통증이 생겼다.
긍정적 강화 훈련은 통제된 상황에서 동물이 겪는 스트레스를 오히려 키운다.
글쓴이가 막대기로 발을 건드리며 "foot"이라고 하자 Molly는 발을 들어 올렸다.
탈수된 새들은 높은 기온이 도시의 물 공급원을 말려 매년 떨어진다.

It was amazing to see bears and elephants moving freely in a large field.  Our tasks for the day included cleaning the shelter and preparing food for the animals.  While cleaning the habitats, we checked if there were any hazards that could harm the animals.  Then, we helped prepare the food by cutting up fruits and vegetables and dividing them into several large baskets.  For old elephants with weak teeth, we chopped bananas instead of the sugarcane that they usually eat.  Spending the whole day helping out with the animals was an incredible experience for me.  It was a rewarding experience, and I was impressed with the attention the staff members gave to all the animals.  July 30, Tuesday Today, we did something special for Ben and Lily.  These two baby bears were rescued after they had been raised illegally in a tiny cage on a farm for many years.  To help the bears restore their natural instincts, we carried out some special activities known as “behavioral enrichment. ” For example, we made honey-log feeders for the bears.  First, we made several holes in a log and filled them with honey.  Then, we hung the honey-log feeders on trees near the bears’ habitat.  As bears are intelligent and curious creatures, they can become bored and stressed when lacking mental and physical stimulation.  The honey-log feeders stimulate their natural curiosity and keep them as active as they would be in the wild.  After a while, Ben and Lily approached the feeders and started eating the honey inside.  They are so cute!  July 31, Wednesday This morning, we had the opportunity to learn about animal treatment thanks to Molly, an elderly elephant.  After spending 25 years carrying tourists along rough roads, she developed a twisted spine and foot pain.  In order to support Jane in taking care of Molly’s foot, we took part in positive reinforcement training, which involves using rewards to encourage desirable behaviors.  When I gently touched her foot with a pole and called out, “foot,” she lifted it.  We then rewarded her with a sweet piece of watermelon, her favorite fruit.  This training helps reduce the stress that animals experience during controlled situations, such as treatment or a health examination.  The good news is Molly seems to be adapting well, and I expect her to get better soon.  August 1, Thursday On the last day, we were called to the rescue center due to a sudden emergency.  Some dehydrated birds had fallen out of the sky in the city and were brought to the center.  Following the veterinarian’s guidance, we provided water to the birds while the vets treated their broken wings and legs and injected them with vitamins for a speedy recovery.  It was shocking that this type of accident happens every year since the high temperatures dry up water sources in the city. Saying goodbye to the animals and staff, I felt grateful for the opportunity to volunteer.  From this experience, I learned the importance of treating animals with respect and care.  I also came to realize that humans are just another kind of animal and share the Earth with all other living creatures.  To improve animal welfare, I’ll work hard with Care for Animals members.

questions.stem: 다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 [조건]에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 영작하시오. (영어로) "나는 그녀(Molly)가 곧 나아지기를 기대한다." [조건] (1) I, better, expect, get, her, soon, to 를 모두 사용할 것 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 나는 그녀(Molly)가 곧 나아지기를 기대한다
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- 핵심은 '나는 기대한다'라서 주어 I + 동사 expect로 시작해요.
- expect는 'expect + 목적어 + to부정사(~가 …하기를 기대하다)' 구조를 써요. 그래서 her(목적어) + to get(to부정사)이 이어져요.
- '나아지다'는 get better, '곧'은 soon.
- 순서: I + expect + her + to get + better + soon → I expect her to get better soon (7단어)
det.tip: expect + 목적어(her) + to부정사(to get) 구조를 기억하세요.
